summary: Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev worked in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy, Keown earned a B.A. from Lancaster University and a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford. In 1995, he became Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London.

A scholar of Indology and history/archaeology, Kosambi studied at Harvard under George David Birkhoff. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1931), Fergusson College (1932), and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

Arnold specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago. He taught at McGill University (2003–2004) and served as Assistant Professor of Philosophy of Religion at the University of Chicago (2004–2011).
Dan Li works in linguistics and Buddhist studies, having studied under Sherab Gyatso. She is attested as an Associate Professor at Soka University in 2026.

Lusthaus is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at Temple University. His academic posts include positions at Grinnell College (1988–1989), Florida State University (attested 1997), and Harvard University (2005).

A specialist in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Martin earned his Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington under Elliot Sperling and others. His appointments include positions at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters (~1995–1996) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1996).

Working in religious studies and Tibetology, Smyer Yü received his PhD from the University of California, Davis. He served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his PhD at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and a Dr.phil. at the University of Copenhagen. He has served as a professor at Copenhagen since 2002 and at the University of Oxford (2018–2021).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Getz earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He is attested as an associate professor at Bradley University in 2019.
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Daniel Amadé Scheidegger completed his doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology, Stevenson earned his Ph.D. from Columbia University. He served as an assistant professor at Butler University (attested 1986) and at the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003).
Working in history, archaeology, and Japanology, Borengasser earned a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley.

Boucher works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology, earning his doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair. He has held positions as an Associate Professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008 and 2026).
Waugh specializes in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Yale and Harvard Universities before joining the faculty at the University of Washington in 1972.

Gilman studied at Yale, Harvard, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution for Science (1902–1904).

Cozort specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, completing his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He held posts at Bates College (~1986–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988–2021).
Specializing in religious studies, Indology, and history/archaeology, Dubuisson served as a director of research at CNRS and Charles de Gaulle University – Lille III around 1988.

A scholar of Indology and philosophy, Ingalls studied at Harvard University under Walter Eugene Clark and Willard Van Orman Quine. He served as a professor at Harvard (~1949–1983), including as Wales Professor of Sanskrit (attested 1980–1992).
